subdomain: 2.5 Implement prompt reuse strategies (caching, modular prompts, Skills)

en.question: Three report-generating services copy the same instruction text, and corrections now reach only some copies. Each service also has its own output contract and request-specific evidence. The immediate goal is consistent maintenance, not lower API processing time. Which reuse approach best addresses that goal?

options.text: Version shared instructions centrally; compose each service's output rules and request evidence separately.
options.note: Shared ownership removes duplicated maintenance while preserving distinct service contracts and data roles. This is a prompt-management design, not an automatic cache or instruction-following guarantee.

options.text: Enable prompt caching independently for each copied prompt and use cache hits as proof that policy corrections are synchronized.
options.note: Caching reuses exact submitted prefixes; it does not update the source copies. Divergent prompts can each have successful cache hits.

options.text: Merge every service's output rules into one universal prompt and let the model infer the intended service from the evidence.
options.note: This hides the output-contract selection inside inference and can introduce conflicts. Reuse should preserve explicit service-specific requirements instead of relying on incidental request content.

options.text: Append the newest correction after each service's old instructions without resolving contradictions in the shared policy.
options.note: Append-only patches keep multiple competing statements of the policy. They do not establish one maintainable authoritative version across services.

references.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
